/-!
# Erdős Problem 552

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/552](https://www.erdosproblems.com/552)
- [BEFRS89] Burr, S. and Erdős, P. and Faudree, R. J. and Rousseau, C. C. and Schelp, R. H., Some
  complete bipartite graph-tree Ramsey numbers. Graph theory in memory of G. A. Dirac (Sandbjerg,
  1985) (1989), 79-89.
-/

namespace Erdos552

/--
Determine the Ramsey number
$$R(C_4, S_n),$$
where $S_n=K_{1,n}$ is the star on $n+1$ vertices.

A problem of Burr, Erdős, Faudree, Rousseau, and Schelp [BEFRS89].

This problem is #19 in Ramsey Theory in the graphs problem collection.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_552.parts.i :
    ∀ (n : ℕ),
      SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)
        (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 1) (Fin n)) =
        answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

/--
In particular, is it true that, for any $c > 0$, there are infinitely many $n$ such that
$$R(C_4, S_n) \leq n + \sqrt{n} - c?$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_552.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (c : ℝ), 0 < c →
      Set.Infinite {n : ℕ |
        (SimpleGraph.graphRamsey (SimpleGraph.cycleGraph 4)
          (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin 1) (Fin n)) : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) + Real.sqrt n - c} := by
  sorry

-- TODO: Add variants of the problem.

end Erdos552

reformulations.difference: BEFRS89 §4 says “for every constant c”; Lean restricts the constant to positive real numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any real c, choose d = max(c, 1). Then d > 0 and d ≥ c, so infinitely many inequalities R(C₄,Sₙ) ≤ n + √n − d imply infinitely many inequalities with c. The converse is immediate by restriction to positive constants. This equivalence was proved for an arbitrary real-valued sequence in the scratch file.

review.notes: Both declarations agree with the cited primary paper. Checked answer types and scope, ordinary rather than induced graph containment, star indexing, and real-valued arithmetic. Finite Ramsey theory ensures that graphRamsey's defining set is nonempty. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean and compute.lean verify the graph definitions, R(C₄,S₀)=1, and exclusion of n=0 from part ii. Exhaustive small computations give Ramsey numbers 1, 4, 4, 6 for n=0,1,2,3. The live erdosproblems.com page and forum returned HTTP 403 despite descriptive User-Agent headers; the full cited paper was read instead. The current community database lists #552 as open, consistent with both category tags.
